title: CLAT Practice Set 2
pageDesc: Free CLAT practice paper set 2 with detailed solutions.

questions.text: In a passage the author writes: "Had the policy been implemented earlier, the crisis would have been averted." Which hidden premise must the author assume for this counterfactual to be logically valid?

options.label: A
options.text: The policy was the only factor influencing the crisis.

options.label: B
options.text: All other variables remained constant (ceteris paribus).

options.label: C
options.text: The crisis would have occurred regardless of the policy.

options.label: D
options.text: The policy was implemented later than planned.

questions.solution: Correct answer: All other variables remained constant (ceteris paribus)..

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following best describes an implicit assumption in an argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A stated reason supporting the claim.

options.label: B
options.text: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold.

options.label: C
options.text: A counterargument presented for refutation.

options.label: D
options.text: A statistical evidence cited by the author.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold..

questions.text: A candidate encounters an inference question where one option is factually true in the real world but not supported by the passage. According to the Principle of Passage‑Only Reasoning, how should this option be treated?

options.label: A
options.text: Select it because it is factually correct

options.label: B
options.text: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage

options.label: C
options.text: Select it if it aligns with the candidate's domain knowledge

options.label: D
options.text: Mark it as correct only if the passage does not contradict it

questions.solution: Correct answer: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage.

questions.text: Paragraph 1 cites a single study showing a 12% rise in test scores after a policy change. Paragraph 3 reveals the study had a small sample and short duration. The author concludes the policy is universally effective. This conclusion is:

options.label: A
options.text: Supported by the evidence presented.

options.label: B
options.text: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later.

options.label: C
options.text: Irrelevant to the study’s findings.

options.label: D
options.text: Strengthened by the later paragraph’s details.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later..

questions.text: For a question stem “All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT,” the most efficient method described in the passage is:

options.label: A
options.text: Choose the option that is false in the real world.

options.label: B
options.text: Locate evidence for each option in the passage; the one lacking support is the answer.

options.label: C
options.text: Select the option that contains the strongest hedging language.

options.label: D
options.text: Pick the longest option.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Locate evidence for each option in the passage; the one lacking support is the answer..

questions.text: What is the typical practice of major international translation prizes regarding the distribution of prize money?

options.label: A
options.text: The prize is awarded solely to the translator.

options.label: B
options.text: The prize is split between the translator and the author, or both receive equal recognition.

options.label: C
options.text: The prize is awarded solely to the author.

options.label: D
options.text: The prize money is donated to a literary foundation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The prize is split between the translator and the author, or both receive equal recognition..

questions.text: The Supreme Court struck down the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) in the Fourth Judges Case (2015) primarily because:

options.label: A
options.text: It violated the seniority convention for appointing the Chief Justice of India

options.label: B
options.text: The inclusion of the Law Minister and two eminent persons impaired the primacy of the judiciary, violating the basic structure

options.label: C
options.text: It failed to provide adequate representation for women and marginalized communities

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment procedure under Article 368 was not followed correctly

questions.solution: Correct answer: The inclusion of the Law Minister and two eminent persons impaired the primacy of the judiciary, violating the basic structure.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines the 'Almost Right' trap as described in the passage's section on Diagnostic Answer-Option Forensics?

options.label: A
options.text: An option that uses high-frequency passage vocabulary to exploit familiarity heuristic

options.label: B
options.text: An option that contains a verifiably true statement from the passage but fails the question's specific demand

options.label: C
options.text: An option that applies a statutory interpretation canon outside its proper jurisdictional domain

options.label: D
options.text: An option that infers causation from a historical correlation without corroborating evidence

questions.solution: Correct answer: An option that contains a verifiably true statement from the passage but fails the question's specific demand.

questions.text: A pre‑Constitution statute regulating motor vehicle permits was inconsistent with Article 19(1)(g) when the Constitution came into force. In 1960, a constitutional amendment removed the inconsistency. The statute became enforceable again without fresh legislation. Which doctrine explains this revival?

options.label: A
options.text: Doctrine of Eclipse

options.label: B
options.text: Doctrine of Severability

options.label: C
options.text: Doctrine of Pith and Substance

options.label: D
options.text: Doctrine of Basic Structure

questions.text: Which body explicitly names the lead agency for a United Nations International Year?

options.label: A
options.text: The UN Secretariat.

options.label: B
options.text: The General Assembly through its resolution.

options.label: C
options.text: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

options.label: D
options.text: The Secretary‑General.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The General Assembly through its resolution..

questions.text: Which case marked the beginning of the shift in locus standi by recognizing that a letter addressed to a judge could be treated as a writ petition?

options.label: A
options.text: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979)

options.label: B
options.text: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)

options.label: C
options.text: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987)

options.label: D
options.text: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984)

questions.solution: Correct answer: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981).

questions.text: The passage lists several common traps in advanced reading comprehension. Which of the following is explicitly identified as a trap?

options.label: A
options.text: Confusing the author's tone with the tone of a cited expert.

options.label: B
options.text: Over-inferring from limited evidence.

options.label: C
options.text: Failing to identify the main idea of each paragraph.

options.label: D
options.text: Misreading complex vocabulary.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Over-inferring from limited evidence..

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) from a sovereign microstate?

options.label: A
options.text: SARs have full external sovereignty like microstates.

options.label: B
options.text: SARs lack external sovereignty but possess internal autonomy.

options.label: C
options.text: Microstates lack internal autonomy but have external sovereignty.

options.label: D
options.text: Both SARs and microstates are full UN members with identical rights.

questions.solution: Correct answer: SARs lack external sovereignty but possess internal autonomy..

questions.text: Which factor is a stronger indicator of a capital city's diplomatic hub status than the number of embassies?

options.label: A
options.text: Number of consulates.

options.label: B
options.text: Presence of permanent secretariats and recurring summit cycles.

options.label: C
options.text: Size of the foreign ministry.

options.label: D
options.text: Volume of tourist arrivals.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Presence of permanent secretariats and recurring summit cycles..

questions.text: Which case established that judicial review of constitutional amendments is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution, leading to the striking down of a clause that sought to curtail such review?

options.label: A
options.text: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)

options.label: B
options.text: Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967)

options.label: C
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

options.label: D
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980).
